newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors bet on Hughes buyout.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors bet on Hughes buyout.

text.p: Call option activity on Hughes Electronics Corp suggested investors were betting that the unit would be sold off, traders said Thursday.
Stock and options trading picked up Thursday after a report that Hughes's parent General Motors Corp had received two bids for Hughes's defense operations, traders said.
Hughes shares were up 1-3/4 at 62-7/8 by 1200 CST/1800 GMT on about 1.3 million shares.
The Wall Street Journal reported that GM had received a $9 billion bid from Raytheon Co and a higher bid from Northrop Grumman Corp for the Hughes defense unit.
General Motors and Raytheon declined to comment on the report.
"There's a fair amount of call buying, which is in my opinion saying people believe there will be a deal," one trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said.
Among the calls, the February 60 traded about 1,390 contracts, the January 60 traded 1,245 and the January 55 traded 1,040.
The most active Hughes put was the January 60, which traded a mere 130 contracts.
The trader at the CBOE said some of the call volume was probably from investors taking profits as call premiums rose along with the stock.
The January 60 call, for instance, rose 1-1/8 to three and reached a high of 3-3/4.
The January 55 call added 2-3/8 to 8-1/2 and the February 60, which still has six weeks to go until expiration, rose 5/8 to 4-5/8. It reached a session high of 5-3/8.
January contracts expire at the end of next week.
Traders said volatilities in the Hughes options were at historically high levels.
Volatility in the February calls was in the mid-30 region, up from around 31, one trader said.
Options on both Raytheon and Northrop were relatively inactive although the Raytheon February 50 and 55 calls each traded around 100 contracts.
Raytheon shares fell 1-3/4 to 47 and Northrop shed 1-3/8 to 77-7/8.
